rationale: A wins because it knows the difference between an angle and a fantasy. It explicitly refuses "Canva's recent AI acquisition is already powering its enterprise suite," while B turns the same unsupported leap into a kept angle: "Canva bought an AI image-generation startup — now it's the engine inside an enterprise pitch." A has one sloppy overreach with "220 million free users," but its strongest frames are grounded, distinct, and press-shaped.
gaps_in_A: "220 million free users" is not in the update; the fact is 220 million monthly users, not necessarily free users.
The counterposition and governance angles still need a named enterprise customer; A admits this, but without one the launch risks staying in roadmap-story territory.
"legal and brand teams will allow" is plausible enterprise framing, but the supplied facts only say brand controls and admin tools, not legal review or compliance workflows.
gaps_in_B: "now it's the engine inside an enterprise pitch" asserts the acquired startup powers the product; the update does not say that.
"The acquisition and the AI-powered Enterprise launch are being connected in the same announcement" is not supported by the provided facts.
"Adobe Firefly and Microsoft Designer" adds specific competitor-product claims not given in the update.
The next step, "newsjack-detector," is the wrong move for a launch-based pitch set; the useful next step is proof gathering and journalist fit, especially a named customer.
